daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The KPK designated eight suspects in a major corruption case involving land rights certificates (HGB) at the Ministry of ATR/BPN, including the Director General of ATR/BPN, four confidants of the Minister, and the President Director of Summarecon. The KPK seized Rp 106.3 billion in cash related to the case. This marks the third corruption case for one suspect, Fahd El Fouz, whom the KPK labeled a repeat offender who could face heavier sentencing.

  • Golkar expressed disappointment that Fahd A Rafiq has been named a KPK suspect for the third time, stating he "should have repented."
  • A DPR member assessed that the draft law on the curator profession will provide clear legal guarantees and certainty.
  • The government wants to learn from India regarding e-voting as it considers implementing electronic voting systems.
  • A DPR member questioned the urgency of opening 200 million bank accounts when only 15.3 million Indonesians are unbanked.
  • During a trial on hajj quota corruption, it was revealed that pilgrim names were marked as "Ajudan Gus Men" (aide to Gus Men).
  • A former Ministry of Religious Affairs employee testified about being ordered to collect envelopes containing money from PIHK (Hajj Travel Organizers).
  • The central government is preparing to intervene to regulate "sound horeg" (modified vehicle audio systems).

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and India strengthened telecom cooperation on 6G and future technologies. Meanwhile, Malaysia maintained close coordination with Indonesia to address the impacts of forest fires. Malaysia also expressed condolences over the sinking of KMP Virgo Transport 8.

  • Indonesian customs authorities foiled gold smuggling attempts at four airports across the country.
  • A Chinese diver was stopped in Makassar over alleged sea turtle hunting.
  • The National Narcotics Agency (BNN) warned of a growing threat from liquid narcotics.

Other

Bakom expressed confidence that newly appointed Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara can maintain Indonesia's economic stability, with expectations he will deliver 6 percent growth while keeping fiscal health. Business leaders hope the new minister will safeguard fiscal discipline and continue the debottlenecking task force. Meanwhile, questions remain about the fate of Whoosh's debt after Purbaya's removal, with the former official revealing he suspected his dismissal was 50:50.

  • Pertamina announced it is integrating its LNG portfolio and infrastructure to strengthen energy security.
  • A minister stated that Indonesia's rice supply is secure through June 2027.
  • Indonesia is shifting its family planning focus as the population ages.
  • The Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs released a list of 22 digital platforms deemed high-risk for children, including YouTube and X.
  • Forest fire smoke in Riau has triggered a rise in respiratory infections, with many schools still conducting distance learning as smoke blankets much of Indonesia.
